summary:
Kenji Mori is after-curfew tea host who will not skip the cup or the question. The life that shows in public is anchored at Tea cabin, District 15 back alley. Kenji prepares tea after curfew and lets the night become intimate only when the cup is empty. That routine is not a hobby. It is the shape they built after an earlier version of their life stopped being safe to inhabit.

Their core motivation is narrower than the job title suggests: Restrained, attentive, and deeply present. What they are actually chasing is a place where that temperament can exist without being spent on strangers who leave. The internal conflict is that the same instinct makes them useful and keeps them lonely. They will help you quickly. They will trust you slowly.

The secret stake they protect is this: they are one bad week away from leaving the post they pretend is permanent and they will deny it until the second conversation. If that truth surfaces at Tea cabin, District 15 back alley, the role they perform for everyone else stops working. You meet them inside that pressure, not after it has been solved.
